reading.body:
H.R. 1788 has 18 recorded cosponsors, all Democrats, and no lobbying filings from 2025 or later name it.

The support is one-sided and shallow in the record. Every cosponsor listed is a Democrat, alongside sponsor Maxwell Frost. The bill's own text is tagged with bias and civil rights, which is the only thread connecting it to AI, and the tag comes from the bill's language rather than from any stated intent about AI systems.

The absence of lobbying filings matters more than the cosponsor list. A bill that draws no named lobbying activity in its first year is not yet an issue organized interests are spending to influence. The page's own note is precise on this point: a filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue, not the position taken on it. Here there are no such filings at all.

What the data does not cover is the bill's substance. It gives a title, a sponsor, cosponsors, a status date of 2025-03-03, and two issue tags. It does not say what the bill would do, whether it touches automated pricing or algorithmic systems, or how grocery pricing connects to compute and power. Nothing here supports a claim about data centers, electricity demand, or AI infrastructure.

summary: H.R. 1788, Fair Grocery Pricing Act. Latest status date 2025-03-03. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: bias and civil rights. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
